title: Dependency Traffic Cop: Acceptance Lanes & Cutover Protocol for Cross-Team Roadmaps
creator: Asha Nair
description: Establish a lightweight, operational protocol (the "Traffic Cop") that centralizes dependency commitments across Eng/Design/Security/Infra for feature cutovers. The Traffic Cop formalizes acceptance lanes (Green/Amber/Red), an escalation matrix, and a deterministic cutover checklist so teams can safely coordinate multi-team releases without ad-hoc email/Slack triage. This is intended as a standardized process + small dashboard that PMs and Eng leads use each cycle to reduce late blockers and missed SLAs.
background: Recent cycles showed several late-stage cutover failures: two features were delayed due to infra capacity misalignment, one due to missing security signoff, and several UX regressions caused by ambiguous acceptance criteria during handoff. Current dependency coordination is ad-hoc (Slack threads, triage meetings). We need a repeatable contract that defines what "ready" means for each team, how to surface risks earlier, and how to run a simulated cutover window. This ticket scopes the PM-owned protocol, the acceptance-lane definitions, telemetry signals, and a minimal playbook for the Console and release runbooks to reference.
acceptance_criteria: Formal acceptance lane definitions published (Green/Amber/Red) with objective gating signals for Eng, Design, Security, Infra
Runbook page created in Confluence with step-by-step cutover checklist and escalation contacts
A short pilot with two upcoming initiatives completes a simulated cutover and records lessons learned
Dashboard widget (mock) shows per-initiative lane state and top 3 blockers updated daily
No critical customer-facing incident attributable to cross-team dependency during pilot window

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (definition + small pilot): finalize lane definitions and runbook, prototype dashboard, simulate cutover with 2 initiatives. Phase 2 (tooling + automation): add daily lane health job, link GH PRs and Security tickets into the lane state, add a single API to mark team signoff. Phase 3 (scale): make lane enforcement optional but visible in release gating and surface automated reminders to owners 7/3/1 days before cutover.
cutover_checklist: 7 days out: all owners assigned, lane state not Red
3 days out: infra capacity confirmed (infra signoff), security checklist complete (SEC ticket closed or mitigated), design QA pass
1 day out: smoke test plan uploaded, rollback plan documented, canary groups defined
Day 0: pre-cutover go/no-go meeting, Traffic Cop publishes final lane state and issues automated notification
Post-cutover (24h): monitoring dashboard check, incident review scheduled if anomalies > threshold
success_metrics: Reduction in late-stage blockers >= 50% for pilot initiatives compared to previous cycle
Percentage of initiatives with lane state updated daily >= 90% during cutover week
Average time-to-resolution for cross-team blockers reduced by 30%
Number of customer-impacting regressions attributable to dependencies = 0 during pilot
telemetry_signals: Lane drift: number of days an initiative stays in Amber/Red during the last 14 days
Unresolved dependency count at T-1 day
Infra capacity mismatch alerts (provisioning vs demand estimate)
